title: 东坡
author: 苏轼
intro: After the rain, when the townspeople have gone home, an exiled poet walks his rough hillside path alone by moonlight — and loves the clack of his walking stick on the stones.
analysis: 这首诗写苏轼在黄州东坡夜里散步。东坡是他被贬到黄州后亲手开荒种地的一块山坡，他也因此自号“东坡居士”。第一句写雨后的东坡，月光格外清亮。第二句说：城里的人都走光了，只剩下我这个“山野之人”还在走。第三、四句是全诗的重点：别嫌坡上的路坑坑洼洼、高低不平，我偏偏喜欢手杖敲在石头上发出的“铿铿”声。表面写走路，其实写人生——路不好走（就像他被贬的处境），他却能从里面找到乐趣。城里的喧闹散去，只剩下手杖的声音，诗也就格外安静。这种乐观、豁达的态度，正是苏轼最让人喜欢的地方。
analysisEn: Su Shi wrote this about a night walk on the East Slope at Huangzhou — the hillside plot he cleared and farmed with his own hands after being exiled there. He liked it so much that he took “Dongpo” (East Slope) as his pen name. The first line shows the slope just washed by rain, the moonlight unusually clear. In the second, the townspeople have all gone home and only he, a “man of the wilds”, is still out walking. The last two lines carry the meaning: don’t complain that the path is rough and stony — he actually enjoys the sharp clack of his stick against the rocks. On the surface it is a walk; underneath it is about life. The road is hard, like his exile, yet he finds pleasure in it. Notice, too, how much the poem is about sound: after the noise of the town fades, the only thing left is the ring of the stick. That cheerful, open-hearted attitude is exactly why Su Shi is so loved.
background: Su Shi (1037–1101), also called Su Dongpo, was the great all-round talent of the Song — poet, essayist, painter and calligrapher. Exiled to Huangzhou (1080–1084) after a political trial over his poems, he farmed the East Slope and wrote this short poem there.
pronunciation: 荦确 luò què（山石高低不平的样子）；铿然 kēng rán；曳杖 yè zhàng。行尽 xíng jìn、野人行 xíng。机器朗读“荦确、曳”容易读错，已在“朗读用字”列换成同音字，音频需人工听验。
version: 采用通行文本（《苏轼诗集》）。

lines.py: yǔ xǐ dōng pō yuè sè qīng
lines.lit: Rain washes the East Slope; the moonlight is clear.
lines.en: Rain has rinsed the East Slope; the moonlight is clean and clear.

lines.py: shì rén xíng jìn yě rén xíng
lines.lit: The town people have all gone; the country man walks.
lines.en: The townsfolk have all gone home; now the man of the hills walks out.

lines.py: mò xián luò què pō tóu lù
lines.lit: Don’t dislike the rough, stony path on the slope;
lines.en: Don’t grumble that the hillside path is rough and stony —

lines.py: zì ài kēng rán yè zhàng shēng
lines.lit: I myself love the clanging sound of my trailing stick.
lines.en: I love the clack of my stick on the stones.

words.note: 苏轼在黄州开垦的坡地，后来成了他的号“东坡”。
古义指住在乡野的人，这里是苏轼自称；今天“野人”指未开化的人，意思不同。
莫：不要；嫌：嫌弃，现代汉语“嫌麻烦”。
形容山石不平，今天不用。
曳：拉、拖，现代汉语“摇曳”；杖：手杖。

imagery.name: 雨
imagery.zh: 一场雨把东坡洗得干干净净，月色也更清，暗示心境的清明。
imagery.en: The rain washes the slope clean and clears the moonlight — a hint of the poet’s clear, calm mind.

imagery.name: 月
imagery.zh: 清亮的月光陪着诗人独自散步，显得宁静而自在。
imagery.en: Clear moonlight keeps the lone walker company — quiet and free.

imagery.name: 路
imagery.zh: 高低不平的坡头路象征坎坷的人生，诗人却偏爱走在上面的声音。
imagery.en: The rough hillside path stands for a hard life — and he chooses to enjoy the sound of walking it.
